issues.legal_issue: A vendor is a necessary party to a suit seeking specific performance of a sale agreement where the property has subsequently been transferred to another purchaser.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought specific performance of an agreement against the original vendor and subsequent purchasers.
The requested conveyance could require the vendor to give effect to terms of the original agreement, while the subsequent purchasers would join to pass their title.
The plaintiffs also sought, in the alternative, repayment of amounts from the vendor.
issues.conclusion: The vendor was a necessary party because the conveyance required his participation and the alternative monetary relief could not be granted in his absence.
issues.legal_principle: A decree for specific performance should put the purchaser in the position they would have occupied had the contracting parties completed the sale; the vendor must therefore join in the conveyance, while a subsequent transferee joins to pass the title vested in them. The Court applied Lala Durga Prasad v. Lala Deep Chand, [1954] S.C.R. 360, and R. C. Chandiok v. Chuni Lal Sabharwal, [1971] 2 S.C.R. 573. It also relied on the need for the vendor's presence to grant alternative relief against the vendor.

predicates.specific_performance_case: The proceeding seeks specific performance of an agreement to sell property that has been transferred to a subsequent purchaser.
predicates.vendor_is_to_execute_conveyance: The original vendor must participate in executing the conveyance, including to give effect to terms of the original sale agreement.
predicates.alternative_repayment_is_sought_from_ven: The claimant seeks repayment of money from the original vendor as alternative relief.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance case requires the vendor to execute the conveyance and seeks alternative repayment from that vendor, the vendor is a necessary party.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal cannot proceed as a whole after it abates against a deceased respondent when deciding the remaining appeal would require inconsistent decrees or leave necessary relief unavailable, and the general appellate power to vary a decree for the benefit of parties does not cure that problem.
material_facts: The appeal was brought by subsequent purchasers against a decree for specific performance that required payment jointly to the vendor and the subsequent purchasers.
The plaintiffs had also sought substantial alternative monetary relief against the vendor.
The vendor died while the appeal was pending, and the application to substitute the vendor's legal representatives was dismissed.
Setting aside the specific-performance decree would affect the joint decree, and the alternative monetary relief could not be granted without the vendor or the vendor's legal representatives.
issues.conclusion: The abatement concerning the vendor was fatal to the entire appeal; Order 41, Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure did not allow the appeal to proceed, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 22, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an appeal abates as against a deceased party when the required legal representatives are not brought on record. Under State of Punjab v. Nathu Ram, [1962] 2 S.C.R. 636, abatement makes the decree between the appellant and the deceased respondent final and prevents its direct or indirect modification. Rameshwar Prasad v. M/s Shyam Beharilal Jagannath, [1964] 3 S.C.R. 549, and Pandit Siri Chand v. M/s Jagdish Parshad Kishin Chand, [1966] 3 S.C.R. 451, support the rule that an appeal cannot continue where it is not properly constituted or its success would produce inconsistent decrees. Order 41, Rule 4 cannot overcome those problems where reversing the decree would affect a joint decree or required relief against the deceased party cannot be granted.

rule.if: appeal_case and respondent_dies_during_appeal and legal_representatives_not_substituted_in_time and (relief_would_modify_joint_decree or success_would_create_inconsistent_decrees or necessary_relief_unavailable_without_deceased_party)

predicates.appeal_case: The proceeding is an appeal from a decree.
predicates.respondent_dies_during_appeal: A respondent dies while the appeal is pending.
predicates.legal_representatives_not_substituted_in: The deceased respondent's legal representatives are not brought on record within the required time.
predicates.relief_would_modify_joint_decree: The relief sought on appeal would require changing a decree made jointly in favour of the deceased party and other parties.
predicates.success_would_create_inconsistent_decree: Allowing the appeal while the deceased party's decree remains final would result in inconsistent decrees concerning the same subject matter.
predicates.necessary_relief_unavailable_without_dec: The court cannot grant relief required to resolve the dispute without the deceased party or their legal representatives.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a deceased respondent whose legal representatives were not substituted in time, and granting the appeal would modify a joint decree, create inconsistent decrees, or leave necessary relief unavailable, the entire appeal is incompetent.
